title: Low-field MRI-derived synthetic CT is tested in liver treatment replanning
summary: In 37 liver cases, U-Net-generated synthetic CT images from low-field MRI were evaluated in retrospective treatment replanning. Both loss-function variants met the reported planning objectives in this source cohort. The study does not establish clinical equivalence, independent deployment safety or patient benefit.
ai_technology: U-Net with MSE and VGG16-based perceptual loss

evidence.tested: The 37 patients supplied 2,561 liver-region image slices. Ten-fold evaluation grouped patients, leaving 3–4 people out per fold. Synthetic images generated for held-out cases were compared with each patient’s original CT in target/organ-at-risk planning. Perceptual and MSE variants had mean absolute image errors of 35.64 and 35.67 HU, and all synthetic-CT plans met the source planning objectives.
evidence.unknown: The same small single-system cohort informed preliminary training choices, so this is not an external independent validation. Missing fine structures such as ribs and registration between separately acquired MRI/CT remain limitations. Reported nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests, and visual image quality is not delivered-dose safety. Manual target contours were transferred from original CT; an entirely CT-free clinical workflow was not tested. No actual treatment-outcome comparison or demonstrated clinical benefit is reported. The August 2021 online version is represented; its issue date is 2022.
evidence.ai_role: Learned MRI-to-CT synthesis supplied images for a defined dosimetric reference comparison; conventional treatment-planning software computed the plans.

source_review.scope: Original computational training/partition Methods, represented applied Results and relevant limitations actually read; no source code executed.
